summary: 11 findings. The service has no OpenTelemetry code at all: no SDK, no provider, no exporter, no instrumentation package in go.mod.
Highest priority is the SDK bootstrap plus HTTP server spans named by chi route pattern and database/sql client spans; together they make per-request query fan-out (N+1) visible in a trace waterfall.

Every hot handler issues queries in loops (nearby-chairs, notification chair stats, ride history, owner sales), and the schema has no secondary indexes, so DB spans are the main diagnostic signal for this service.
The outbound payment gateway call retries up to 5 times with 100ms sleeps inside an open DB transaction; it needs client spans and retry visibility.
No route-aware chi instrumentation exists in opentelemetry-go-contrib; route names must come from chi's RoutePattern applied onto otelhttp spans.
The internal matching endpoint (polled every 0.5s) and slog error logging are recommended follow-ups once the baseline is in place.
flow: audit -> select -> instrument -> verify -> configure/dashboard -> publish

evidence.finding: Go 1.23 module; go-chi/chi/v5 v5.1.0, go-sql-driver/mysql v1.8.1, jmoiron/sqlx v1.4.0, oklog/ulid/v2. No go.opentelemetry.io dependency.
Single HTTP process; setup() opens sqlx DB and builds chi router, main() calls http.ListenAndServe(:8080) with no shutdown handling
19 routes registered with Go 1.22 method patterns on chi; three auth middlewares wrap app/owner/chair groups
Each authenticated request runs one SELECT by access_token (no index on access_token)
Payment gateway calls via http.DefaultClient with retry loop (max 5, 100ms sleep)
Matching runs as GET /api/internal/matching, polled every 0.5s by a curl sidecar
log/slog default handler (stdout) in writeError; chi middleware.Logger access log to stdout
Dockerfile builds with plain go build; compose runs nginx, webapp, mysql:8, matcher sidecar
Only primary keys; no secondary indexes on rides.user_id/chair_id, ride_statuses.ride_id, chair_locations.chair_id, *.access_token
No *_test.go files; only go build / go vet are available locally

signal_flow.component_flow_map: process main.go [GAP: SDK bootstrap and resource identity] -> chi router + auth middleware [GAP: HTTP server spans by route] -> handlers -> sqlx/database/sql -> MySQL [GAP: Database query spans] ; handlers -> connection pool [GAP: DB connection pool metrics] ; POST /api/app/rides/{ride_id}/evaluation -> http.DefaultClient -> payment gateway [GAP: Payment gateway client spans] ; writeError -> slog stdout [GAP: Error attribution on spans] [GAP: Local OTLP application logs] ; matcher sidecar -> GET /api/internal/matching [GAP: Matching outcome visibility] ; Go runtime [GAP: Go runtime metrics] ; handlers loops [GAP: Handler business-step spans] ; POST /api/initialize -> init.sh [GAP: Initialize step visibility]

findings.title: No OpenTelemetry SDK, exporter, or service identity
findings.gap: go.mod has no go.opentelemetry.io dependency and main.go creates no TracerProvider, MeterProvider, propagator, or resource. http.ListenAndServe has no shutdown path, so buffered telemetry would be lost on container stop.
findings.impact: No signal can leave the process; nothing appears in Splunk Observability for isuride.
findings.product_outcome: The isuride service should appear in the service map with a stable service.name and deployment environment, and buffered spans should flush on stop.
findings.required_fix: Add an otel.go that builds TracerProvider and MeterProvider with OTLP exporters configured only from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* env vars, a resource from OTEL_SERVICE_NAME/OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES with default service.name=isuride, the W3C TraceContext+Baggage propagator, and flush/shutdown on SIGTERM via http.Server.Shutdown.
acceptance_criteria: Spans and metrics export over OTLP to the endpoint given by env with service.name=isuride.
OTEL_SERVICE_NAME and OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES override defaults and are not overwritten.
SIGTERM triggers provider ForceFlush/Shutdown before exit.
constraints: Do not hardcode the OTLP endpoint.
Keep a no-OTel build path possible (the measurement plan compares instrumented vs uninstrumented builds).

expected_telemetry.name: service.name=isuride
expected_telemetry.product_view: APM service map and service filter

expected_telemetry.name: OTLP trace/metric exporter from env
expected_telemetry.product_view: Data arriving in Splunk Observability Studio

follow_up_actions: After instrumentation, confirm isuride appears in Splunk Observability Studio service list.

findings.title: HTTP requests have no route-named server spans
findings.gap: The chi router has only middleware.Logger and Recoverer. No otelhttp handler wraps it. The official contrib repository has no chi instrumentation (the otelchi path in the contrib map does not exist), so route names must be taken from chi.RouteContext(...).RoutePattern() after routing.
findings.impact: Operators cannot see which of the 18 endpoints is slow or failing during a benchmark, and ride/chair IDs in paths would explode cardinality if raw paths were used.
findings.product_outcome: Each request should appear as one server span named like 'GET /api/app/nearby-chairs' or 'POST /api/app/rides/{ride_id}/evaluation', with route-level latency, rate, and error charts.
findings.required_fix: Wrap the chi router with otelhttp.NewHandler (go.opentelemetry.io/contrib/instrumentation/net/http/otelhttp) and add a small chi middleware that, after next.ServeHTTP, sets http.route and the span name from chi RoutePattern. otelhttp also emits http.server.request.duration.
acceptance_criteria: Server span name and http.route use the chi pattern, never a path containing a ride ID.
http.server.request.duration has http.route, http.request.method, http.response.status_code.
Auth middleware DB query is a child of the server span.
constraints: Do not add the community riandyrn/otelchi when otelhttp plus RoutePattern is sufficient.
follow_up_actions: Filter traces by http.route in Splunk Observability Studio after a bench run.

findings.title: Database queries are invisible inside requests
findings.gap: sqlx.Connect uses the raw mysql driver; no database/sql instrumentation. Handlers issue queries in loops: appGetNearbyChairs (all chairs x rides x latest status), getChairStats per notification, appGetRides per ride (status, coupon, chair, owner), ownerGetSales per chair.
findings.impact: The dominant cost of this service (query fan-out and missing indexes) cannot be localized; a slow request looks like one opaque block.
findings.product_outcome: A trace for GET /api/app/nearby-chairs should show every SELECT as a child span, so repeated identical queries (N+1) are visible at a glance.
findings.required_fix: Open the DB with github.com/XSAM/otelsql (otelsql.Open with semconv mysql attributes) and wrap with sqlx.NewDb so all sqlx Get/Select/Exec and transactions emit client spans with parameterized db.query.text; pass ctx through. Note db.Beginx() calls drop ctx; switch to BeginTxx(ctx, nil) so transaction spans stay in the request trace.
acceptance_criteria: Each SQL statement in nearby-chairs appears as a child span of the server span.
db.query.text contains placeholders only; bound argument values are not recorded.
Transaction Begin/Commit spans share the request trace.
constraints: Span name must be low cardinality (operation + table), not the full query.
follow_up_actions: Open a nearby-chairs trace during bench and count child SELECT spans.

findings.title: Connection pool saturation has no signal
findings.gap: The pool runs with database/sql defaults (MaxIdleConns=2, unlimited open). Local runs failed with 'connect: cannot assign requested address' from connection churn, and nothing in the app exposed pool state.
findings.impact: Pool exhaustion or churn surfaces only as unexplained 500s.
findings.product_outcome: A chart should show open/idle/in-use connections and wait time during the bench, making connection churn visible before errors appear.
findings.required_fix: Register otelsql.RegisterDBStatsMetrics for the DB handle to emit db.client.connection.* metrics.
acceptance_criteria: db.client.connection.count by state and db.client.connection.wait_time datapoints export every interval.
constraints: Do not change pool sizing as part of instrumentation; that is a performance change to be measured separately.
follow_up_actions: Compare pool chart against error rate during bench.

findings.title: Payment gateway calls and retries are untraced
findings.gap: requestPaymentGatewayPostPayment uses http.DefaultClient with no transport instrumentation and retries up to 5 times with 100ms sleep, while the caller holds an open DB transaction.
findings.impact: Latency of POST /api/app/rides/{ride_id}/evaluation cannot be split between DB and the payment upstream; retries are silent; no trace context reaches the gateway.
findings.product_outcome: The evaluation trace should show POST /payments client spans (and GET /payments on failure) with the retry count, so upstream slowness is distinguishable from DB time.
findings.required_fix: Use an http.Client with otelhttp.NewTransport for payment calls and record the attempt number on each client span (or a span event per retry).
acceptance_criteria: Client spans for POST /payments are children of the evaluation server span.
A retry produces a distinct span or event with the attempt number.
traceparent header is sent upstream.
constraints: Do not record the Authorization header or token.

expected_telemetry.name: POST
expected_telemetry.product_view: Trace waterfall: upstream call inside evaluation

follow_up_actions: Inspect an evaluation trace for the payment child span.

findings.title: Error responses are not attributed on spans
findings.gap: writeError(w, status, err) has no request context, so the error cannot be recorded on the active span. It also calls slog.Error(msg, err) with a bare error, which produces '!BADKEY=' output instead of a named attribute.
findings.impact: 5xx spans would show status only, without the cause (e.g. 'cannot assign requested address'); 4xx business errors like 409 'ride already exists' are indistinguishable.
findings.product_outcome: Error traces should carry the error message and type, so the cause of 500s is visible from the trace list without reading container logs.
findings.required_fix: Pass r.Context() into writeError (or a request-aware variant) and call span.RecordError and span.SetStatus(codes.Error) for 5xx; log with slog.ErrorContext(ctx, msg, "error", err).
acceptance_criteria: A forced DB error yields a server span with status Error and an exception event.
4xx responses do not set span status Error.
constraints: Mechanical signature change only; response bodies stay identical.
follow_up_actions: Filter traces by error=true after a failing run.

findings.title: Application logs are stdout only, without trace correlation
findings.gap: log/slog uses the default handler; no LoggerProvider, no otelslog bridge, no trace_id/span_id in records. No OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER or logs endpoint is configured.
findings.impact: Error logs cannot be joined to the trace that produced them.
findings.product_outcome: slog error records should appear in local Splunk Observability Studio linked to their trace, while stdout output stays as is.
findings.required_fix: Add a LoggerProvider with an OTLP log exporter targeting the local Splunk Observability Studio receiver, bridge slog via go.opentelemetry.io/contrib/bridges/otelslog fanned out with the existing stdout handler, honor OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=none, and shut down with the other providers.
acceptance_criteria: One OTLP log record per slog call with trace_id/span_id inside a request.
stdout output unchanged.
OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=none emits no OTLP log record.
constraints: Never send logs to a cloud endpoint from this change.
Do not export the chi access log twice.
follow_up_actions: Open the log linked from an error trace.

findings.title: Matching results are invisible
findings.gap: internalGetMatching returns 204 for every outcome (no waiting ride, no free chair after 10 random tries, matched). It runs ORDER BY RAND() plus a completion subquery up to 10 times per call.
findings.impact: The bench penalises long waits for matching; without an outcome signal you cannot tell whether matching runs but fails to find chairs or never sees rides.
findings.product_outcome: A chart should show matching outcomes per minute (matched / no_waiting_ride / no_free_chair) and attempts per call.
findings.required_fix: Set a low-cardinality matching.outcome attribute and attempts count on the server span, and add a counter isuride.matching.outcomes{outcome} plus histogram isuride.matching.attempts.
acceptance_criteria: Each matching call records exactly one outcome value.
Attempts histogram reflects the loop count (1..10).
follow_up_actions: Correlate matching outcomes with bench 'waiting for match' dissatisfaction.

findings.title: Loop-heavy handlers lack step spans
findings.gap: getChairStats, calculateDiscountedFare, and getLatestRideStatus are called per row inside loops; with DB spans alone, the waterfall shows hundreds of flat siblings with no grouping by step.
findings.impact: Readers see 'many queries' but not which helper multiplies them.
findings.product_outcome: Traces should group repeated queries under named step spans like getChairStats, with a loop item count attribute.
findings.required_fix: Add internal spans around getChairStats, calculateDiscountedFare, and getLatestRideStatus callers' loops with a low-cardinality item count attribute.
acceptance_criteria: Step spans parent their DB spans.
Item counts recorded as attributes, never IDs.
constraints: Span names are function names, never IDs.
follow_up_actions: Compare grouped vs flat waterfall in the demo.

findings.title: Go runtime health is not exported
findings.gap: No runtime instrumentation; goroutine count, heap, and GC pauses are unavailable.
findings.impact: CPU or GC pressure from instrumentation overhead itself cannot be observed.
findings.product_outcome: Charts should show goroutines, heap, and GC for isuride alongside request latency.
acceptance_criteria: go.goroutine.count, go.memory.used, go.memory.gc.goal datapoints export.
follow_up_actions: Use runtime charts when measuring instrumentation overhead.

findings.title: Initialize step timing is opaque
findings.gap: POST /api/initialize shells out to ../sql/init.sh (schema + data reload) with no span around the exec.
findings.impact: Initialize time counts against the bench; its duration split is unknown.
findings.product_outcome: The initialize trace should show the init.sh exec as a child span with its duration.
findings.required_fix: Wrap exec.Command("../sql/init.sh") in an internal span with process.exit.code.
acceptance_criteria: One init.sh span per initialize call with exit code.
constraints: Do not capture script output in attributes.
follow_up_actions: Check initialize duration in first bench trace.

anti_patterns: slog.Error("error response wrote", err) passes a bare error as a key, producing !BADKEY output (main.go:175).
db.Beginx() drops the request context, so transactions would start outside the request trace once instrumented (app_handlers.go:195 and other handlers).
The audit library map lists go.opentelemetry.io/contrib/instrumentation/github.com/go-chi/chi/otelchi, which does not exist on the Go module proxy; only community github.com/riandyrn/otelchi exists.
recommendation: Select OTEL-001..OTEL-007 as the baseline, copy the generated prompt, and run $otel-instrument; add OTEL-008..OTEL-011 for the demo narrative.
